verdict.rationale: Inngest's first-party docs describe durable agents in which every step and tool call is checkpointed, so a crashed run resumes from the failed step rather than restarting. Its guides cover ReAct-style agent loops where each iteration is a durable, retriable step, step.ai.wrap() runs AI SDK calls as steps, and default per-step retries are documented. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of crash-resume behavior specifically for LLM agent loops.

support.subject: As an agent builder, I run LLM agent loops as durable workflows — model and tool calls as checkpointed, retried steps that survive crashes mid-run

citations.quote: Every step, every tool call, every decision the agent makes is checkpointed as it happens. If the process dies at step 7 of 12, the agent picks up at step 7 — not step 1.
building a ReAct-style agent loop (Reason → Act → Observe → Repeat) where each iteration is a durable, retriable step
step.ai.wrap() wraps other AI SDKs (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Vercel AI SDK) as a step
so Inngest can memoize results, retry failures independently, and resume long-running work from the last successful checkpoint
By default, in addition to the initial attempt, Inngest will retry a function or a step up to 4 times until it succeeds.
